calculate_subnet.description: Work out everything about an IPv4 subnet from an address and its size: the network and broadcast addresses, subnet and wildcard masks, how many devices it holds and the first and last usable address. Write the size on the address (192.168.1.77/24 or 192.168.1.77 255.255.255.0) or pick it from Subnet size.
calculate_subnet.name: calculate_subnet

parameters.description: An IPv4 address, with or without its size: 192.168.1.77/24, 192.168.1.77 255.255.255.0 or just 192.168.1.77.
parameters.name: address

parameters.description: The subnet's size, if the address doesn't already end in /24 or a mask. Leave it empty for a single address (/32).
parameters.name: prefix_length

parameters.description: Also return the address, masks and range written in binary, octet by octet.
parameters.name: include_binary

address.description: The IP address that was entered.

binary.description: The same details in binary. Empty unless Show binary was turned on.

address.description: The address in binary, octet by octet.

first_assignable_host.description: The first usable address in binary.

last_assignable_host.description: The last usable address in binary.

broadcast_address.description: The last address: the broadcast address.

cidr.description: The address with its prefix, such as 192.168.1.77/24.

first_usable_address.description: The first address a device can use. Empty for a /31 or /32.

last_usable_address.description: The last address a device can use. Empty for a /31 or /32.

network_address.description: The first address: the network itself.

network_cidr.description: The network itself in CIDR notation, such as 192.168.1.0/24.

next_address.description: The address after the one entered, for stepping through a range.

total_addresses.description: How many addresses the subnet holds.

usable_hosts.description: How many addresses can be given to devices (all but the network and broadcast addresses).

wildcard_mask.description: The wildcard mask (the subnet mask inverted), as used in Cisco access lists.

check_spf.description: Check the SPF record that says which servers may send email for a domain: the one a domain publishes, or one you paste in before publishing it. Returns whether each part is valid and how many DNS lookups it needs, since mail servers reject a record that needs more than 10.
check_spf.name: check_spf

parameters.description: Whether to check a domain's published record or one you paste in.
parameters.name: check

parameters.description: The domain whose SPF record to check, such as example.com.
parameters.name: domain

parameters.description: The record to check, starting v=spf1, such as v=spf1 mx include:_spf.google.com -all.
parameters.name: spf_record

dns_lookups.description: How many DNS lookups the record needs.

domain.description: The domain checked. Empty when a pasted record was checked.

found.description: Whether the domain publishes an SPF record.

invalid_terms.description: The parts of the record that are invalid.

is_valid.description: Whether every part of the record is valid.

spf_record.description: The SPF record that was checked.

terms.description: Each part of the record and whether it is valid.

term.description: The part of the record, such as include:_spf.google.com.

within_lookup_limit.description: Whether it stays within the 10 lookups mail servers allow.

convert_number.description: Convert a whole number between binary, octal, decimal and hexadecimal. Turn on two's complement to convert negative numbers, or to read a binary or hex value as signed.
convert_number.name: convert_number

parameters.description: The whole number to convert, such as 255, 11111111 or ff. Prefixes such as 0x and 0b, spaces and underscores are ignored.
parameters.name: number

parameters.description: The base the number is written in.
parameters.name: from_base

parameters.description: The base to convert it to.
parameters.name: to_base

parameters.description: Off for positive numbers. Pick a width to convert negative numbers: binary and hex results are padded to that many bits.
parameters.name: twos_complement

number.description: The number that was converted, as it was read.

twos_complement_bits.description: The two's complement width used. Empty when it was off.

convert_range_to_cidr.description: Turn an IPv4 range such as 10.0.0.5-10.0.3.200 into the exact list of CIDR blocks that covers it, or merge a list of blocks, ranges and addresses into the fewest blocks. Also returns the single smallest block that covers everything and how many extra addresses it would let in. Use the exact list for firewall rules and allowlists.
convert_range_to_cidr.name: convert_range_to_cidr

parameters.description: One or more IPv4 ranges (10.0.0.5-10.0.0.20), networks (10.0.0.0/24) or single addresses, separated by commas or new lines. Up to 1,000.
parameters.name: ranges

adjusted_entries.description: Entries written with an address inside a network (10.0.0.5/24) that were read as the whole network (10.0.0.0/24).

items.description: An entry as it was written.

block_count.description: How many blocks the exact answer needs.

blocks.description: The exact blocks, with their details.

addresses.description: How many addresses the block holds.

cidr.description: The block in CIDR notation, such as 10.0.0.0/23.

first_address.description: The first address in the block.

last_address.description: The last address in the block.

wildcard_mask.description: The wildcard mask (the subnet mask inverted), as used in Cisco access lists.

cidrs.description: The exact CIDR blocks covering the input, as plain text: ready for a firewall rule or an allowlist.

covering_block.description: The smallest single block covering everything, and what it adds.

addresses.description: How many addresses the block holds.

cidr.description: The block in CIDR notation, such as 10.0.0.0/23.

extra_addresses.description: Addresses in the single block that were not in the input.

extra_percent.description: Those extra addresses as a percentage.

extra_ranges.description: Where the extra addresses are (up to 50 ranges).

first_address.description: The first address in the block.

is_exact.description: Whether the single block holds exactly the input and nothing more.

last_address.description: The last address in the block.

wildcard_mask.description: The wildcard mask (the subnet mask inverted), as used in Cisco access lists.

covering_cidr.description: The smallest single block that contains every input address.

first_address.description: The lowest address in the input.

last_address.description: The highest address in the input.

total_addresses.description: How many distinct addresses the input covers.

encode_text.description: Encode text as Base64, Base64URL or URL (percent) encoding, or decode it back.
encode_text.name: encode_text

parameters.description: The text to encode or decode.
parameters.name: text

parameters.description: Which encoding to use.
parameters.name: encoding

parameters.description: Whether to encode the text or decode it.
parameters.name: direction

get_tls_certificate.description: Read the TLS/SSL certificate a site is serving right now: who it was issued to and by, when it expires (and in how many days), every name it covers, and whether it covers the hostname you asked about. Use it to watch for expiring certificates or to confirm a renewal went live.
get_tls_certificate.name: get_tls_certificate

parameters.description: The site to check, such as example.com. A pasted web address works too.
parameters.name: hostname

parameters.description: The port the site serves TLS on. Leave it at 443 for a website.
parameters.name: port

covers_hostname.description: Whether the certificate covers the hostname that was checked.

days_until_expiry.description: Whole days until it expires. Negative once it has.

is_valid_now.description: Whether today is inside its validity dates.

issued_by.description: The certificate authority that issued it.

issued_to.description: The name the certificate was issued to.

pem.description: The certificate itself, in PEM format.

lookup_dns.description: Look up the DNS records published for a hostname: IPv4 addresses (A), aliases (CNAME), mail servers (MX), name servers (NS), the start of authority (SOA) and text records (TXT). A name with no records comes back with found set to false rather than failing, so a workflow can check whether a domain resolves.
lookup_dns.display_str_template: Look up the DNS records for {0}.
lookup_dns.name: lookup_dns

parameters.description: The hostname or domain to look up, such as example.com or www.example.com. A pasted web address works too.
parameters.name: hostname

parameters.description: Which record types to return. Leave empty for all of them.
parameters.name: record_types

canonical_names.description: The names this hostname is an alias of (CNAME).

found.description: Whether any records of the chosen types were found.

hostname.description: The hostname that was looked up.

mail_servers.description: The mail servers (MX), lowest priority number first.

priority.description: Its priority: lower is tried first.

records.description: Every record found, one row each.

priority.description: The mail server's priority, for MX records.

ttl.description: How many seconds the record may be cached, for A records.

type.description: The record type: A, CNAME, MX, NS, SOA or TXT.

value.description: The record's value: an address, a host name or the text.

soa.description: The start of authority record. Empty when SOA was not included.

hostmaster.description: The administrator's mailbox, written as a name.

lookup_whois.description: Look up who a domain is registered through and when it was registered and expires, with the days left until expiry worked out for you. Give it www.example.com and it looks up example.com. Some country domains publish only the registrar.
lookup_whois.name: lookup_whois

parameters.description: The domain to look up, such as example.com.
parameters.name: domain

created_at.description: When the domain was first registered (ISO 8601).

days_until_expiry.description: Whole days until the registration expires. Negative once it has.

domain.description: The registered domain that was looked up. For www.example.com this is example.com.

registrar.description: The company the domain is registered through.

registry_domain_id.description: The domain's ID at the registry.

status.description: The registry status, such as client transfer prohibited.

plan_subnets.description: Divide a network into right-sized subnets for the number of devices each one needs (variable-length subnet masking). Returns the block given to each subnet with its usable range and masks, why that block was chosen, and the space left over as ready-to-use blocks. If they don't all fit, the ones that did are still returned and the rest are listed under did_not_fit.

subnets.explanation: 60 hosts + 2 reserved (network and broadcast) = 62 addresses. The smallest block that holds that is a /26 (64 addresses, 62 usable), leaving 2 spare. It is placed at the start of the parent network.
subnets.name: Sales

subnets.explanation: 2 hosts + 2 reserved (network and broadcast) = 4 addresses. The smallest block that holds that is a /30 (4 addresses, 2 usable), leaving 0 spare. It is placed at the next /30-aligned address after 192.168.1.0/26.
subnets.name: WAN

plan_subnets.name: plan_subnets

parameters.description: The IPv4 network to split up, with its size, such as 192.168.1.0/24. A /30 or larger.
parameters.name: network

parameters.description: Each subnet's name and how many devices it needs, such as Sales: 60. Up to 64 subnets; names up to 32 characters.
parameters.name: subnets

all_fit.description: Whether every subnet asked for fitted in the network.

allocated_percent.description: The share of the network given out, in percent.

did_not_fit.description: Subnets there was no room for. Empty when all_fit is true.

needed_prefix_length.description: The block size it needed, such as /26.

requested_hosts.description: How many hosts were asked for.

free_blocks.description: The space left over, as CIDR blocks ready to use.

items.description: A free block in CIDR notation.

free_percent.description: The share of the network left over, in percent.

free_ranges.description: The space left over, as address ranges.

addresses.description: How many addresses are free here.

network.description: The network that was divided, in CIDR notation.

network_total_addresses.description: How many addresses the network holds.

subnets.description: The subnets that were placed, in address order.

cidr.description: The block given to it, such as 192.168.1.0/26.

explanation.description: Why this block size and position were chosen.

first_usable_address.description: The first address a device can use.

last_usable_address.description: The last address a device can use.

requested_hosts.description: How many hosts were asked for.

spare_hosts.description: Usable addresses beyond what was asked for.

total_addresses.description: How many addresses the block holds.

usable_hosts.description: How many devices the block can hold.

wildcard_mask.description: The wildcard mask (the subnet mask inverted), as used in Cisco access lists.

subnets_requested.description: How many subnets were asked for.

description: Network calculators and lookups from NetworkCalc: work out subnets, plan VLSM address space, turn IP ranges into CIDR blocks, look up DNS, WHOIS and SPF records, read a site's TLS certificate and its expiry date, and convert numbers between binary, octal, decimal and hex or text to and from Base64.
